full_text_en:
Wu Lianda — Case of Contract Fraud

Prosecutorial Authority: Wenzhou City People's Procuratorate, Zhejiang Province.

Defendant: Wu Lianda, male, born October 14, 1971, legal worker at Wenzhou Zhengda Law Office, arrested on December 15, 1999.

The case of defendant Wu Lianda for contract fraud was initiated by the Wenzhou City People's Procuratorate, Zhejiang Province, by filing a public prosecution with the Wenzhou Intermediate People's Court, Zhejiang Province, on July 24, 2000.

The indictment charges that: On October 28, 1998, after learning from Shanghai Sakura Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sakura Company) that Siemens (China) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Siemens Branch) was seeking technical cooperation for 8BK80 switchgear, defendant Wu Lianda agreed with Sakura Company that Sakura Company would sign a contract with Siemens Branch for the 8BK80 technical cooperation, and then Wu Lianda and others would sign a contract with China Great Wall Electric Group Company (hereinafter referred to as Great Wall Company) for the same technical cooperation. To defraud Great Wall Company's trust, on January 9, 1999, Wu Lianda, together with another person, signed an 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement with Great Wall Company in the name of Siemens Branch without authorization, stipulating that Great Wall Company pay a deposit of RMB 800,000. Upon receiving the deposit, Wu Lianda changed the name "Siemens Branch" used without authorization in the agreement to "Sakura Company," and paid RMB 220,000 of the deposit to Sakura Company as a signing fee for the cooperation with Siemens Branch, appropriating the remainder. Because the 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement signed between Sakura Company and Siemens Branch restricted the use of the technology to Sakura Company in Shanghai, it was impossible to provide the technology to Great Wall Company. After Great Wall Company raised objections, Wu Lianda, in order to refuse to return the deposit, unilaterally added a clause to the "Low Voltage Equipment Cooperation Agreement" between Great Wall Company and Sakura Company stating that "the original 8BK80 technical cooperation remains valid, and Great Wall Company may not demand the return of the deposit." Wu Lianda, with the purpose of illegal possession, signed a contract using another's name, defrauding property in an especially huge amount. His conduct already constitutes the crime of contract fraud and should be severely punished.

Defendant Wu Lianda argued in his defense: In entering into and performing the 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement with Great Wall Company based on authorization from Sakura Company, he did not violate legal provisions; it was a lawful business operation. The 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement was a contract between Sakura Company and Great Wall Company and was actually performed. The changes to certain contents of the agreement were made in accordance with Sakura Company's instructions and complied with legal provisions. Great Wall Company's request for return of the deposit lacks factual and legal basis. The RMB 220,000 portion of the deposit was paid to Sakura Company for contract performance, and Sakura Company subsequently entered into relevant agreements with Siemens Branch, also facilitating other cooperation projects between Great Wall Company and Siemens Branch. The economic benefits for Great Wall Company upon full performance of the contract far exceed the deposit. Subjectively, he did not have the intent to unlawfully possess the deposit, and thus his conduct does not constitute the crime of contract fraud.

Defense counsel for defendant Wu Lianda argued: Wu Lianda did not engage in any conduct of signing an agreement under the name of Siemens Branch without authorization, nor did he have the subjective purpose of unlawfully possessing the RMB 800,000 deposit. His conduct does not constitute a crime. The reasons are: (1) There is no basis for the indictment's allegation that Wu Lianda used Siemens Branch's name without authorization. The words "Siemens Company" on the cover of the 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement were a clerical error, which Wu Lianda explained in a corrective letter, and the content of the agreement also indicated that Wu Lianda and others were intermediaries. Persons such as Ye Xiangyao from Great Wall Company stated that Wu Lianda introduced himself as a business agent of Siemens Branch, but there is no other corroborating evidence, so it is insufficient. Relevant letters of appointment, agreements, and Chen Jianhong of Sakura Company all prove that Wu Lianda and others signed the agreement with Great Wall Company on behalf of Sakura Company. (2) Siemens Branch knew that Sakura Company intended to transfer the technology to Great Wall Company. Chen Jianhong of Sakura Company testified that this matter had been communicated to Mr. Baker, the representative of Siemens Branch. The relevant agreements directly signed between Great Wall Company and Siemens Branch, as well as the conduct of transferring drawings and other documents among Great Wall Company, Sakura Company, and Siemens Branch, all prove that Siemens Branch was aware of and actively performing the agreement relationship with Great Wall Company. Absorbing Sakura Company as a member enterprise of Great Wall Group was a means of resolving cooperation obstacles in the performance of the technical agreement between Sakura Company and Great Wall Company, and also proves that the subject of the technical cooperation agreement was Sakura Company. Therefore, Wu Lianda did not engage in any conduct of using Siemens Branch's name without authorization. (3) Wu Lianda did not have the subjective purpose of illegal possession. Wu Lianda's receipt of the RMB 800,000 deposit as an agent under the relevant agreement was lawful. If Wu Lianda had intended to possess the money, he would not have paid RMB 220,000 to Sakura Company, kept RMB 330,000 with Wu Shangzhong, or continued to work and pay expenses to perform the agreement. The procuratorial authority's presumption that Wu Lianda's use of the deposit constituted appropriation has no legal basis.

The Wenzhou Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found the following facts:

In July 1998, defendant Wu Lianda, while serving as a legal advisor to Wenzhou Ruili Fitness Sports Products Co., Ltd., learned from Chen Jianhong, General Manager of Sakura Company, during business dealings with the company's director Wu Shangzhong, about the information regarding Siemens Branch's transfer of 8BK80 technology. He subsequently negotiated cooperation matters with one company, but it fell through. After Great Wall Company learned of this, it decided to have its Vice General Manager Wang Yaqun, using her friendship with Wu Lianda, offer more favorable conditions to strive for the project's signing. To this end, the parties held multiple contacts and negotiations concerning the deposit amount, technology usage fees, annual production volume, and other matters. On December 28 of that year, Sakura Company formally appointed Wu Shangzhong as its business manager for the Wenzhou area and Wu Lianda as deputy manager, and they agreed in writing: Sakura Company would sign an agreement with Siemens Branch, with costs paid by Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda; Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda would sign a cooperative production agreement with Great Wall Company; a fee of RMB 6,800 per unit would be charged, with Sakura Company receiving RMB 800 and Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda receiving RMB 6,000; Great Wall Company's future orders for circuit breakers and other components from Siemens Branch would be handled by Wu Lianda through Sakura Company. Thereafter, Wu Lianda, based on the 8BK80 switchgear technical consultation agreement text provided by Sakura Company between itself and Siemens Branch, drafted a technical cooperation agreement, writing on the cover that Great Wall Company (Party A) and Siemens Company (Party B) were the parties to the agreement, and also added "SIEMENS" at the header of each page. On January 8, 1999, Ye Xiangyao, Chairman of Great Wall Company, and Wang Yaqun went to Shanghai and visited Wu Shangzhong's Hetai Company and Sakura Company, learning that Chen Jianhong was a business agent of Siemens Branch. On January 9, Ye Xiangyao, representing Party A, and Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda, representing Party B, signed the 8BK80 switchgear technical cooperation agreement at the Hetai Company office. The agreement stipulated that Siemens Branch, through Party B, would decide to transfer technical drawings to Party A; Article 4 of the agreement stipulated that Party A would pay Party B a technology usage fee of RMB 6,800 for each switchgear produced, calculated at a minimum of 100 units in the first year, and at least 180 units from the second year onward, with the excess paid according to the actual amount; Article 5 stipulated that within one week after the agreement was signed, Party A must pay Party B a deposit of RMB 800,000, which would be fully refunded by Party B upon completion of the agreement, and if Party A violated any term, the entire deposit would be forfeited; Article 22 stipulated that disputes would be submitted to the Wenzhou Arbitration Commission for arbitration. Party B was signed and sealed by Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda, with no other official seals.

On January 13, 1999, Great Wall Company sent an employee to deliver a promissory note of RMB 800,000 to Wu Lianda and collected a receipt and Wu Lianda's corrective letter regarding the agreement. The main contents of that letter were: (1) The technical cooperation agreement was signed by Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda on behalf of Sakura Company; the words "Siemens Company" on the cover were a clerical error. (2) The content of the agreement should be based on the agreement signed between Siemens Branch and Sakura Company. (3) Great Wall Company would not pay additional technical consultation fees. Articles 4, 5, and 22 of the agreement must be performed; other clauses were terminated. (4) Matters concerning Great Wall Company's 8BK80 and low-voltage complete set projects must be confirmed in writing by Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda before reaching an agreement with Sakura Company; otherwise, it would be deemed a breach by Great Wall Company. (5) For cooperation on low-voltage complete set projects, Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda would do their best to urge Sakura Company to facilitate a direct agreement between Great Wall Company and Siemens Branch. If there were objections, a reply must be given within three days; otherwise, it would be deemed acceptance. No additional supplements or amendments would be made. On January 14 and 15 of that year, Wu Lianda withdrew RMB 220,000 from the RMB 800,000 deposit from the bank, paid RMB 220,000 to Sakura Company via promissory note on January 19, paid RMB 20,000 in cash, deposited RMB 330,000 with Wu Shangzhong for safekeeping, and kept the remaining RMB 250,000 himself. On January 27 of that year, Sakura Company signed an 8BK80 switchgear technical consultation, framework, and procurement agreement with Siemens Branch. This agreement included provisions restricting the production site of the cooperation project to Shanghai, confidentiality of information and materials, and technology transfer. On February 1999, Sakura Company paid Siemens Branch RMB 160,000 in technical consultation fees. On February 10, Siemens Branch transferred the technical drawings and related documents for the 8BK80 project to Sakura Company. On February 20, Wu Lianda delivered the drawings and other documents to Great Wall Company, which refused to accept them.

On April 8, 1999, Siemens Branch notified Sakura Company in writing that the agreement had taken effect, requiring arrangements for relevant technical, sales, and business personnel to proceed with specific negotiations for cooperation matters. To ensure that Great Wall Company could produce the 8BK80 switchgear without Sakura Company breaching its contract, after consultation, Great Wall Company agreed to absorb Sakura Company as a member enterprise of the Great Wall Group. Sakura Company also agreed to transfer the low-voltage complete set electrical equipment cooperation project from Siemens Branch to Great Wall Company for negotiation, and an agreement was reached. This agreement stipulated that after Great Wall Company signed an agreement with Siemens Branch, Great Wall Company would pay Sakura Company an intermediary fee of RMB 200,000; if the cooperation failed, the fee would be returned in full. After drafting this agreement, Great Wall Company delivered it to Wu Lianda, who signed it as Sakura Company's representative and sent it to Sakura Company for signature and sealing. However, Wu Lianda added clauses relating to the 8BK80 project to this agreement, which, in addition to content substantially similar to the corrective letter, also included "Great Wall Company shall not demand a refund of the deposit for any reason." Chen Jianhong also signed and sealed the amended agreement. Wu Lianda did not deliver the amended agreement to Great Wall Company for retention. On June 30, 1999, Great Wall Company, on the ground that Wu Lianda had failed to perform the agreement, demanded in writing that he return the deposit. Wu Lianda refused. On January 14, 2000, Great Wall Company signed a framework and procurement agreement concerning switchgears with Siemens Branch, followed by a technical consultation agreement for producing the 8BK80 switchgear. On May 11 of that year, the parties further signed a supplementary agreement to the 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement.

After the case was discovered, Wu Shangzhong has returned RMB 330,000 to Great Wall Company.

The main evidence to confirm the above facts is as follows:

1. Statements of defendant Wu Lianda. Wu Lianda admitted negotiating and signing the 8BK80 technical cooperation project with Great Wall Company as a representative of Sakura Company together with Wu Shangzhong; the text of the agreement was provided by Chen Jianhong, and it was amended after negotiations with Great Wall Company; he drafted the corrective letter and delivered it to Great Wall Company; he added 8BK80 content to the low-voltage agreement; after receiving RMB 800,000, he paid RMB 220,000 to Sakura Company, delivered RMB 330,000 to Wu Shangzhong, and kept the remainder himself; Great Wall Company's request for return of the deposit was without proper grounds, and the right to return the deposit was with Wu Shangzhong and Chen Jianhong, so he did not return it; he confirmed facts such as Great Wall Company visiting Shanghai for an on-site inspection before signing, having no objection to the corrective letter, and then notifying Sakura Company to sign with Siemens Branch; after signing, Sakura Company paid consultation fees of RMB 160,000 and obtained drawings and materials; Great Wall Company refused to accept copies of drawings and materials because it did not obtain the right to use Siemens Company's name.

2. Testimony of witness Wu Shangzhong. He testified that he and Wu Lianda negotiated and signed the 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement with Great Wall Company as business agents of Sakura Company in Wenzhou. The content of the agreement was provided by Sakura Company, and Wu Lianda made amendments; the 8BK80 technical agreement with Great Wall Company was signed at Hetai Company after Ye Xiangyao and others came to Shanghai; of the RMB 800,000 deposit, RMB 220,000 was paid to Sakura Company to purchase drawings, RMB 330,000 was kept by him, and the remainder was with Wu Lianda; the deposit was required due to concerns that the cooperating entity might not pay technology usage fees; after completion, profits were to be divided among himself, Wu Lianda, and Chen Jianhong.

3. Testimony of witnesses Ye Xiangyao, Ye Xiangtao, and Wang Yaqun. They respectively testified to negotiating the 8BK80 technical cooperation agreement with Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda, visiting Sakura Company in Shanghai, and signing the agreement at Hetai Company. Chen Jianhong informed them that business matters were to be handled by Wu Shangzhong. They paid RMB 800,000 to Wu Lianda. Wang also testified to refusing to accept the copies of drawings and materials delivered by Wu Lianda.

4. Testimony of witness Chen Jianhong. He testified to appointing Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda as business agents for the development of the 8BK80 project, providing the agreement text to Wu Lianda, who finalized it. He knew that Wu Shangzhong and Wu Lianda had received the deposit, paid RMB 220,000 to Sakura Company, and received RMB 20,000 in cash. They signed a low-voltage technology transfer agreement with Great Wall Company. In July 1999, Siemens Branch signed a cooperation agreement with Great Wall Company.

5. Agreements, letters of appointment, etc. They prove that Sakura Company appointed Wu Shangzhong as its business manager for the Wenzhou area and Wu Lianda as deputy manager; they signed a cooperative production agreement for 8BK80 switchgears with Great Wall Company, responsible for relationship coordination, agreement performance supervision, and settlement of accounts; the division of technology usage fees; Sakura Company was not responsible for Wu Shangzhong's and Wu Lianda's expenses; and Sakura Company was an agent of Siemens AG, Germany.

6. Technical cooperation agreement. This proves the time and content of the 8BK80 technical consultation agreement signed by Ye Xiangyao with Wu Lianda and Wu Shangzhong, that Party B on the cover was Siemens Branch, and that "SIEMENS" appeared at the header of each page.

7. Copy of corrective letter, letter of introduction, and receipt slip. They prove the content and time of the corrective letter and the fact that it was delivered to Yang Yi, an employee of Great Wall Company, for collection.

8. Receipt, promissory note. They prove the amount, currency type, and time of the deposit paid by Great Wall Company to Wu Lianda.

9. Receipt from Sakura Company. It proves receipt of RMB 160,000 from Wu Lianda for transfer of 8BK80 technical drawings and RMB 40,000 for circuit breaker payments.

10. Two agreements. They prove that Sakura Company was willing to transfer the Siemens low-voltage complete set electrical equipment cooperation project to Great Wall Company for negotiation, and that within 15 days after Great Wall Company signed an agreement with Siemens Branch, Great Wall Company would pay Sakura Company an intermediary fee of RMB 200,000 (RMB 50,000 already prepaid). Wu Lianda added content related to 8BK80 to this agreement, bearing Wu Lianda's seal. It also includes the requirement that Sakura Company pay Wu Lianda an intermediary fee of RMB 80,000 within seven days after receiving the remaining RMB 150,000, and the time for such payment.

11. Agreements, invoices, and copies of drawing and document delivery certificates. They prove the time, content, production location, and technical consultation fee amount of the 8BK80 technical consultation, framework, and procurement agreements signed between Sakura Company and Siemens Branch.

12. Agreements between Great Wall Company and Siemens Branch. They prove that the two companies have signed the 8BK80 technical consultation and low-voltage switchgear framework procurement agreements and their contents.

The above evidence was presented and cross-examined in court, and neither the prosecution nor the defense raised any objections. The evidence corroborates each other and should be confirmed.

The Wenzhou Intermediate People's Court held that:

Article 224 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a person who, for the purpose of illegal possession, uses a fictitious entity or the name of another person in the course of entering into a contract, thereby defrauding the other party of property in a relatively large amount, commits the crime of contract fraud and shall be punished.

Defendant Wu Lianda was engaged by Sakura Company as its business agent in Wenzhou to negotiate the 8BK80 technology transfer agreement with Great Wall Company. After Great Wall Company sent personnel to Shanghai for an on-site inspection, it signed the relevant agreement with Wu Lianda and others. Subsequently, Wu Lianda sent a corrective letter clearly stating that "Siemens Company" on the agreement was a clerical error and that his identity was a business agent of Sakura Company. Great Wall Company raised no objection and did not immediately demand the return of the deposit. After the agreement was signed, Sakura Company signed the relevant technology agreement with Siemens Branch. Sakura Company also transferred the low-voltage complete set project to Great Wall Company to negotiate directly with Siemens Branch. Ultimately, both technology cooperation projects reached agreements. At the same time, after receiving the RMB 800,000, Wu Lianda paid RMB 220,000 to Sakura Company and deposited RMB 330,000 with Wu Shangzhong for safekeeping. This indicates that Wu Lianda subjectively did not have the intent to unlawfully possess the RMB 800,000 deposit. His true purpose was to obtain the technology usage fees payable to him personally under the agreement after Great Wall Company produced the switchgears. Objectively, Wu Lianda did not fabricate an entity or use the name of another person, nor did he fabricate or falsify the 8BK80 technology or the fact of its transfer. After receiving the deposit, he did not squander it or abscond with the money. On the contrary, upon learning that the 8BK80 switchgear was restricted to production only in Shanghai, Wu Lianda actively suggested alternative methods to enable Great Wall Company to achieve production of the product, demonstrating sincerity and concrete actions to perform the contract. Therefore, his conduct does not meet the constitutive elements of the crime under Article 224 of the Criminal Law and does not constitute the crime of contract fraud. The charge brought by the prosecutorial authority is not established. The arguments of Wu Lianda and his defense counsel that Wu Lianda's conduct does not constitute a crime are valid and should be adopted.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 162(2) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment was rendered on January 16, 2001, as follows:

Defendant Wu Lianda is acquitted.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, the Wenzhou City People's Procuratorate, Zhejiang Province, filed a protest. The reasons were: The content of the agreement signed between defendant Wu Lianda and Great Wall Company was not genuine and lacked feasibility for performance. Wu Lianda used Siemens Branch's name without authorization when signing the agreement with Great Wall Company, sent a corrective letter to amend the subject of the agreement, tampered with the stipulated content of the agreement, and refused to return the remaining RMB 250,000 deposit. This shows he subjectively had the intent to unlawfully possess the RMB 250,000 deposit, and objectively committed the act of using Siemens Branch's name without authorization to defraud Great Wall Company of property, thereby constituting the crime of contract fraud. The original judgment was erroneous in fact-finding and inappropriate in the application of law. The protest requested that Wu Lianda be convicted and punished for the crime of contract fraud.

Defense counsel for Wu Lianda agreed with the original judgment, arguing that Wu Lianda did not objectively use fraudulent means to defraud others of property; he entered into the contract with Great Wall Company under his true identity and actively performed the contract; subjectively, he did not have the purpose of possessing the deposit. Counsel requested that the protest be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

The Zhejiang High People's Court, upon trial, finds:

The facts found by the original trial court were corroborated by the testimony of witnesses Ye Xiangyao, Wang Yaqun, Chen Jianhong, Yang Yi, Wu Shangzhong, et al.; the agreement and employment letter signed between Yinghua Company and Wu Lianda and others; the technical cooperation agreement and amendment letter signed between Wu Lianda and others and Changcheng Company; Changcheng Company's letter of introduction for receiving legal documents; the receipt for RMB 800,000; the invoice from Yinghua Company; the document by which Changcheng Company accepted Yinghua Company as a member enterprise; the agreement between Yinghua Company and Changcheng Company on the low-voltage complete-set project; the agreement, invoice, drawings, and documents signed between Yinghua Company and Siemens Branch; Changcheng Company's notice requesting the return of the security deposit; the agreement between Changcheng Company and Siemens Branch; Changcheng Company's certification; and the seizure and return list. Wu Lianda's confession was consistent with the circumstances reflected in the above evidence. The facts of this case are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient.

Defendant Wu Lianda, engaged by Yinghua Company as its business agent in the Wenzhou area, negotiated with Changcheng Company regarding the transfer of the Siemens 8BK80 technology project. At the time of signing the contract, Wu Lianda was unaware that the transfer of this technology was subject to territorial restrictions, which would affect the performance of the agreement with Changcheng Company. Changcheng Company, after directly contacting Yinghua Company and understanding the relationships among the parties and the specific circumstances of the 8BK80 technology transfer, signed the contract with Wu Lianda and others and paid the security deposit, and subsequently raised no objection to the agreement. Wu Lianda made continuous efforts to facilitate the successful transfer of the 8BK80 technology project to Changcheng Company; when obstacles arose to the transfer, he actively promoted Yinghua Company becoming a member enterprise of Changcheng Company, thereby enabling Changcheng Company to obtain the Siemens Branch technology project through an alternative arrangement. Furthermore, throughout the entire process of the low-voltage project technical cooperation between Changcheng Company and Siemens Branch, Yinghua Company consistently recognized Wu Lianda as its business agent in the Wenzhou area, acknowledged his intermediary role, and agreed to his share of the intermediary fees.

The Zhejiang High People's Court held the following opinion:

Defendant Wu Lianda negotiated and signed the agreement with Changcheng Company according to his arrangement with Yinghua Company. However, during the mediation process, he violated the principle of good faith, and in an attempt to enhance his own standing, he repeatedly used Siemens as the subject on the cover and in the content of the agreement, creating the impression that he represented Siemens Branch, and then made corrections after the agreement was signed. Moreover, he unilaterally inserted additional terms into the low-voltage complete-set project agreement signed by Changcheng Company and Yinghua Company. The aforementioned fraudulent conduct was corroborated by corresponding evidence, and the original trial court made corresponding findings of fact. The procuratorial authority's objection raised in the protest regarding this part is well-founded. However, taking the case as a whole, although some of Wu Lianda's actions in signing and performing the technical cooperation agreement on behalf of Yinghua Company with Changcheng Company were somewhat deceptive, subjectively he did not have the intent to illegally appropriate Changcheng Company's property by deceptive means. Wu Lianda's direct motive in signing the contract with Changcheng Company was the hope that the relevant technical cooperation project of Siemens Branch could be successfully transferred, thereby enabling him to obtain a high transfer fee. Objectively, as a business agent of Yinghua Company, Wu Lianda had a certain ability to perform the contract and demonstrated good faith and concrete actions toward its performance. His refusal to return the security deposit was due to specific reasons and was not an attempt to defraud Changcheng Company of its property. His conduct did not fall within the scope of the circumstances described in the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Fraud Cases, such as "knowingly lacking the ability to perform a contract while using deceptive means to defraud others of property" or "concealing contract security deposits or other property that guarantees contract performance and refusing to return it." Although Changcheng Company was misled by certain improper acts of Wu Lianda during the initial negotiations, after investigation and assessment, it ultimately confirmed the possibility of obtaining technical cooperation with Siemens Branch and agreed to sign the contract and make the relevant payments; thus, it was not deceived. Moreover, through the intermediary role of Yinghua Company and Wu Lianda and others, Changcheng Company ultimately achieved the goal of technical cooperation with Siemens Branch and has become a beneficiary. In light of the above, Wu Lianda's conduct does not constitute the crime of contract fraud. The procuratorial authority's protest grounds for convicting and punishing him for contract fraud are insufficient and are not sustained.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Zhejiang High People's Court rendered the following ruling on March 12, 2002:

The protest is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
